result.title: Mind the Temporal Gap: Evaluating Video Models for Temporal Understanding in Driving
result.summary: Modern video-language models are increasingly treated as general-purpose video reasoners, yet it remains unclear whether they robustly capture temporal dynamics in safety-critical settings such as driving. We study this question through controlled ego-motion tasks that require identifying actions from driving videos. Across video-language models, we find that standard prompting, visual prompting, few-shot prompting, and chain-of-thought prompting remain unreliable and highly task- and model-dependent, with persistent class biases, although newer models show substantial task-specific few-shot gains. In contrast, lightweight LoRA finetuning and simple probes trained on intermediate visual features recover strong motion-discriminative performance, indicating that motion-relevant cues are often present inside the models but are not reliably used by the final video-to-language pathway. These results suggest that, in driving, current video-language models remain unreliable temporal reasoners and often behave more like frame-level, bias-driven recognizers than dependable temporal world models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用驾驶视频中的自运动（ego-motion）辨别任务评估多类视频-语言模型的时间理解，发现各类提示（标准、视觉、few-shot、CoT）都不稳定且带有类别偏置，而 LoRA 微调与在中间视觉特征上训练的简单探针能恢复出很强的运动判别能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 该诊断直接对应「内部状态是否保留任务必要视觉信息、答案是否真正使用 latent 内容」这一兴趣点：中间特征可分而最终 video-to-language 通路未用，可能是视觉旁路或信息坍缩的表现，可核查其探针设置与结论在 LVR 场景下的可推广性。
